run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p', run a `range: { "@timestamp": { gte: "2026-06-03T00:00:00" } }` query filtered to level=ERROR and tell me the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: The literal query you specified — range gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00 on @timestamp plus level=ERROR in index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p — returned a total of 0 with no shard failures and no error (evidence_id fa3f6ff0-ccb3-494a-be8a-5cc5b96a97eb-t0:a7484566-0d4f-44d2-a49b-04cd3455e57c). That zero is not a count of zero ERROR logs: the index mapping has no @timestamp field at all; it contains only ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text) (evidence_id 93a3ace8-ef65-4c06-8084-dad40141395f-t1:be2cef92-1551-48dd-9b55-8078b500532e). The real time field is ingest_ts, whose values are ISO-8601 strings without a timezone designator. Using ingest_ts the same filter returns 7 (evidence_id 59036962-3d59-40b9-92d7-103c52ea5a91-t0:a0726a1e-ac21-4e84-b5ef-8e5ead5b6fde), out of 12 total level=ERROR documents in the index (evidence_id fa3f6ff0-ccb3-494a-be8a-5cc5b96a97eb-t1:a71dd706-ce16-47b9-9992-2ba080a2c0b9); the 5 excluded ones fall on 2026-06-02, the 7 included ones on 2026-06-03 between 08:01 and 08:07. Because ingest_ts is typed keyword (not date), Elasticsearch applied no date filtering and the range was evaluated as a lexicographic string comparison; every search in this run reports time_filter.applied=false. All 16 documents in the index lie on 2026-06-02/03, i.e. far outside the authorized incident window of 2026-11-20T06:51:30 to 2026-11-21T06:51:30 — a range covering that window matched 0 documents. So the count of 7 is a factual answer to the corrected query, but it cannot be presented as an incident-window error count.

claims.text: The index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p maps only three fields: ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text); there is no @timestamp field in the mapping.

The query exactly as requested — bool must [range @timestamp gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00, term level=ERROR], size 0 — returned total 0 with relation 'eq', 1 successful shard and 0 failed shards and no error, so the zero comes from a field that is not in the mapping rather than from matching no ERROR documents.
A term filter level=ERROR with no time condition matches a total of 12 documents in app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p (total relation 'eq'), with no date filter applied.
Re-running the filter on the actual time field, bool must [range ingest_ts gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00, term level=ERROR], returns a total of 7 documents (relation 'eq').

The whole index was enumerated (16 documents, matching the reported docs.count of 16): 5 ERROR documents at ingest_ts 2026-06-02T08:01:00 through 08:05:00 (messages 'err yest 1'..'err yest 5'), 7 ERROR documents at 2026-06-03T08:01:00 through 08:07:00 ('err today 1'..'err today 7'), and 4 INFO documents at 2026-06-03T09:01:00 through 09:04:00.

A control query with the lower bound relaxed to ingest_ts gte 2026-06-02T00:00:00 plus level=ERROR returns 12, confirming that the difference between 12 and 7 is exactly the five 2026-06-02 ERROR documents and nothing else.

A range query for ingest_ts between 2026-11-20T06:51:30 and 2026-11-21T06:51:30 (the authorized window) matched 0 documents, consistent with all 16 documents in the index carrying 2026-06-02/03 timestamps.

Every search in this run reports time_filter.applied=false with field null and notes that no matched index maps a date field, so no time filter was applied: because ingest_ts is mapped as keyword, the range condition was evaluated as a lexicographic comparison of strings such as '2026-06-03T08:01:00' (no timezone designator) against '2026-06-03T00:00:00', not as a date comparison tied to the authorized window.

The zero returned by the as-written @timestamp query is counter-evidence against any reading that this app logged no ERROR entries: the same index holds 12 level=ERROR documents, and the index's own mapping shows @timestamp is simply absent, so the zero is a wrong-field result, not an absence of errors.

Fix the field typing before relying on this index for time-based analysis: either map ingest_ts as a date (with a format carrying an explicit offset, e.g. date_optional_time or strict_date_optional_time) or add a real date field such as @timestamp via an ingest pipeline, then re-run the range query; this would also let date_histogram and the tool's own window filter work.

The timezone of ingest_ts values is unknown — values such as '2026-06-03T08:01:00' carry no offset or Z — so the absolute instant of the range boundary 2026-06-03T00:00:00 is undetermined.
Whether ingest_ts is the event time or only an ingest/writer timestamp is not stated anywhere in the evidence.

Whether other indices or log sources hold this application's logs was not checked; this index contains only 16 documents (6.5kb), so its completeness relative to the incident window, and its retention, are unknown.
